claims.claim: A dedication to Robinson precedes Chapter 1
Holmes sits at breakfast while Watson examines a stick left by a visitor
claims.evidence: 'breakfast table. I stood upon the hearth-rug and picked up the stick'

claims.claim: Holmes deduces from 'To James Mortimer, M.R.C.S.' that he is a country doctor, and Mortimer returns
claims.evidence: 'To James Mortimer, M.R.C.S., from his friends of the C.C.H.'; 'a country doctor, as you very astutely observed'

claims.claim: Mortimer tells of a family curse of a spectral hound haunting the Baskervilles; Sir Charles died on the moor
claims.evidence: legend of the hound read by Mortimer; Sir Charles found dead

claims.claim: Sir Henry, the heir, comes from Canada
claims.evidence: 'found that he had been farming in Canada'

claims.claim: Holmes sends Watson with Sir Henry to Baskerville Hall on Dartmoor
claims.evidence: Watson goes to the Hall; Mortimer's address 'Grimpen, Dartmoor, Devon'

claims.claim: Watson meets the Barrymores, the escaped convict Selden, and the Stapletons
claims.evidence: 'Barrymore, the husband acting as butler'; 'Selden, the Notting Hill murderer'; 'introducing you to my sister'
'my name was Selden, and he is my younger brother'; 'his brother-in-law' (mentioned, not part of card)
Holmes joins them on the moor after Watson's reports

claims.claim: Stapleton is a Baskerville kinsman and husband of the woman posing as his sister, using a hound to seize the estate
claims.evidence: 'Rodger Baskerville, the younger brother of Sir Charles, who fled'; 'his sister'... 'my wife brought it'
'Holmes and I both fired together, and the creature gave a...'

claims.claim: Stapleton vanishes into the Grimpen Mire
claims.evidence: 'No one could find his way into the Grimpen Mire tonight'; 'down in the foul slime of the huge morass'

claims.claim: Characters: Stapleton naturalist of Merripit House; Barrymore butler; Mortimer country doctor
claims.evidence: Stapleton's zoology work; Barrymore butler; Mortimer 'typical country practitioner'
